title: Gravitational Field Strength
notes: **Definition:** gravitational field strength $g$ at a point is the gravitational force per unit mass placed at that point: $g = F/m$.
**Field of a point mass:** $g = G\frac{M}{r^2}$, directed toward the mass $M$.
**Near Earth's surface:** $g \approx 9.8\,\text{m/s}^2$. This value varies slightly with latitude and altitude.
**Superposition:** for multiple masses, the total field is the vector sum of the fields from each mass: $\vec{g}_{total} = \sum \vec{g}_i$.
**Units:** N/kg or m/s$^2$. Both are equivalent because $1\,\text{N/kg} = 1\,\text{m/s}^2$.
